goal: Implement configurable assigned capital state engine and eliminate fixed initial capital dependencies from analysis and execution pipeline

contracts.interfaces: export interface AutoTraderState { assignedCapital: number; availableCapital: number; capitalInPosition: number; realizedPnL: number; unrealizedPnL: number; currentPosition: AutoTraderPosition | null; tradingState: string; minTradeCapital: number; maxRiskPerTradePct: number; consecutiveLosses: number; lastUpdated: string; }
function_signatures: executeAutoTraderSell(state: AutoTraderState, exitPrice: number, reason: string): any

execution_steps: Write unit test in frontend/src/__tests__/auto_trader_capital.test.js covering Tests A through H
Run node --test to verify failure on missing autoTraderEngine module
Implement autoTraderEngine.ts with pure state transitions for capital allocation, sizing and compounding
Remove default capital 7.35 hardcode in quantitativeEngine.ts
acceptance_criteria: assignedCapital accepts any positive number without fixed constant defaults
subsequent trade capital reflects realized profit compounding ($100 to $102) and loss deductions ($100 to $97)
capital below minTradeCapital transitions to INSUFFICIENT_CAPITAL with zero trades emitted
serialized state recovers all capital metrics and trading state after restart
definition_of_done: commands.test returns exit code 0 for all 8 mandatory tests
No production code assumes 7.35 as a default or constant

rollback.command: git checkout HEAD -- frontend/src/lib/quantitativeEngine.ts; rm -f frontend/src/lib/autoTraderEngine.ts
